Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{x}^{3}-x\,\text{d}x & =2\int {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x-\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2(\frac{{x}^{3+1}}{3+1})-(\frac{{x}^{1+1}}{1+1})+C \\  & =2(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})-(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
